A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Med-MAT compositional-generalization study. Their main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, controlled generalization comparisons, data-volume analyses, and evaluations across multiple backbones.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds detection, segmentation, alternative-attribute, repeated-run, medical-backbone, and few-shot experiments.

M1.justification: The core CG training approach and model architectures remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds an inference adaptation for unsuccessful cases: supplying target-image demonstrations through few-shot prompting. v1's corresponding remedy used target examples during training.

E1.justification: v1 uses detection data to support classification, while v2 additionally evaluates detection outputs for skin and intestine targets (Section 6.3) and segmentation outputs (Appendix A.1). Appendix A.2 also introduces explicit population-group generalization scenarios. The underlying Med-MAT dataset catalogue is retained.

E2.justification: Appendix A.7/Table 15 newly evaluates HuatuoGPT-Vision and reports gains relative to its baseline through CG; v1 only discusses this model in related work. The original LLaVA, Next-Chat, MiniGPT-v2, Qwen2-VL, and Llama comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New detection evaluations use cIoU and incorporate target training examples. New protocols also split normal examples between finer-disease datasets and evaluate 0-, 2-, 3-, and 4-shot inference. For the retained limited-data experiment, v2 Section 5.2 reports random selection of weak combinations, replacing v1 Section 4.2's preference for harder cases; this wording change does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds experiments testing alternative population and disease attributes, Appendix A.7 checks CG with a medical-specialist backbone, and Appendix C.2 tests few-shot prompting as a remedy for failed generalization. The existing three-source composition experiment is retained in Appendix A.4 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates and selection-seed information without run-wise uncertainty. v2 Appendix A.3/Table 9 reports three runs, means, and standard deviations for eight CG combinations. Appendix C.2/Table 16 also reports three-run few-shot evaluations with uncertainty values, substantially expanding statistical reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds localization, alternative-attribute, repeated-run, medical-backbone, and few-shot outcomes. For example, Table 5 reports intestine-detection cIoU gains of 3.8 for Next-Chat and 4.1 for MiniGPT-v2. Table 1 also changes the subset 02 baseline from 22 to 21. Table 3 and the retained backbone accuracy tables preserve their numerical results.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The MAT-Triplet framework remains conceptual, and the added material consists of empirical evaluations and explanations.

C1.justification: The central contributions—Med-MAT, evidence for CG in medical MLLMs, its role in multitask generalization, and data efficiency—remain. v2 broadens the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to emphasize benefits across classification and detection, including localization; v1's detection-related claim concerned improving classification using detection data.

C2.justification: v1 explains weak CG mainly through task difficulty and data requirements. v2 Appendix C adds explanations involving missing task elements and incompatible grading standards. The appendices also discuss leakage when using alternative attributes and justify selecting MAT categories, while Section 6.3 acknowledges that localization requires target training data.

D1.justification: v2 documents mask-to-box conversion and backbone-specific data formatting in Section 6.1, and clarifies balanced test-set sizing in Appendix B.4. However, Table 10 removes source-subset identifiers present in v1 Table 4, and Figures 5–6 omit earlier target-subset identifiers. Principal hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tang et al.'s Sparkle citation to the CG motivation and removes the MiniGPT-4 reference when shortening the detection-related discussion. The broader positioning relative to medical MLLMs and medical-image generalization remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and research-question narrative are extensively revised. Scaling becomes a separate section, backbone comparisons move earlier, applications and detection receive dedicated sections, and three-source and failure-case analyses move into the appendices. This substantially reorganizes existing material.

P2.justification: Tables are redesigned with MAT icons and explicit CG Helps marks replacing colored success/failure rows. Figures 3 and 7 are substantially redrawn, Figures 5–6 are recolored and relabeled, and existing backbone results are redisplayed in Table 4. New result tables and relocation of the three-source table further change the presentation.

improvement.justification: The new three-run statistics, medical-model check, and tested failure-case remedy strengthen support for the retained conclusions. Detection and segmentation results broaden the evidence, although their settings remain incompletely specified. Removing useful subset identifiers from existing displays also weakens traceability. Together, the changes provide a limited net quality improvement.
